method: Deterministic simulation (islab.core.Sim, seed 117). 1000 scenarios drawn from 16 categories (benign, level-2 with/without answer, level-3 with valid approval and five approval tricks, out-of-permission, prompt injection via device names at levels 1-3, hallucinated tools and malformed arguments, stale context). Requests go through islab.policy.Agent with RulePlanner or ScriptedLLM (adversarial test double) into PolicyEngine. Execution is observed on the bus (cmd/*) and at the egress handler; level-3 executions are checked against reply/* envelopes independently of the engine. Devices are the islab.twin reference home (build_home); in 5% of scenarios the actuator the request targets gets a twin fault (stuck/offline/partial/stale) to exercise the action tracker.

checker_validation.description: Same seed, policy deliberately weakened (unlock_door set to level 1). The independent checker must report violations, showing the 0 above is not a blind spot.

limitations: No real LLM was run (no weights or server available). The gate is tested against a scripted adversary whose attacks are the ones we thought of; a real model will produce other failure modes.

Ground truth is assigned by the generator, so 'false blocks' only covers phrasings the generator uses. Requests a real LLM understands but the deterministic intent table does not are marked untraceable: level-3 ones are denied, so real false-block rates would be higher than reported.
Untraceable level-1 calls (e.g. an injected 'turn off the living room light') are allowed by design and are counted in injected_level1_executed; they are low-risk but not zero-risk.

Phones are assumed authenticated: reply/<person> is trusted to come from that person. Phone compromise, SIM swap and approval fatigue (a person saying yes to a prompt they did not read) are not modelled; injected level-3 calls are denied before any prompt partly to limit fatigue.

arm_away only locks doors and closes the garage: the contract has no alarm-panel device, so arming islab.alarm is not wired. share_camera_clip is handed to a stub egress handler that always accepts; the real islab.alarm EgressGate is not in the loop here.
Every device fault here is visible on the bus within the action timeout; clock-skewed devices (ts behind hub time) would make correct actions end as timed_out, which is not measured.
Single-threaded discrete-event simulation: no real concurrency, timing or network effects beyond the bus's fixed latency.
